text: A long bar in polished durasteel runs the length of the room. Glass shelves four high behind it, lit from below in pale amber. The bartender pours a tall green cocktail and slides it down the bar without looking up.

Black marble floors, gold inlay tracing the path from door to bar. Low conversation, the chime of crystal on crystal, no music. A server collects an empty glass before the patron has finished setting it down.
Curved booths in deep red leather, each angled inward so no patron faces another. Ozone and rosewood. A sommelier presents a bottle table-side with a slight bow and waits for the nod.

Floor-to-ceiling transparisteel walls open onto the skylane traffic two thousand levels down. Low gold light, no overheads. A server lights a dessert at a far table; the flame holds for a measured count and dies.
A grand staircase up to private rooms, brass rail polished to a wet shine. Caf and citrus oil in the air. The maître d' walks a couple up the stairs and does not return for several minutes.

Vaulted ceiling lost in shadow, the room intimate despite its scale. A pianist works through something quiet. Two parents and a daughter in birthday wear share a corner booth, laughing into their water glasses.
Tables spaced for conversation, no two close enough to overlap. The hum of privacy fields under the music. A coaster slides across a table to cover a credit chit, neither patron looking at the other.

Hush of carpet, the soft click of a closing door somewhere. Recessed lighting, every fixture concealed. Two patrons at the bar lean apart the moment a server arrives, and lean back together when she's gone.

Mirrored back-bar, every glass arrangement reflected to infinity. The bartender works without speaking, eyes flicking across the room between pours. The privacy field at booth four flickers, holds, flickers again.

Imperial officers occupy three tables along the south wall, dress greys and quiet talk. A server clears their glasses on a precise rotation. The pianist segues into something older, more measured, without missing a note.
The music cuts. Every privacy field in the room drops at once. The maître d' is at the front, speaking with a man in ISB charcoal, hands clasped at the small of his back.
Conversation continues, slightly too even. The bartender's hands are below the bar. At the central booth, a noblewoman's laugh has cut off mid-syllable; she has not moved since.
An Imperial officer in dress greys nurses a single brandy at the bar, posture immaculate. Switches to formal High Galactic the moment he's addressed — and doesn't notice he does it.
A Bothan in a half-cape watches the lift doors more than her companion, datapad face-down beside her glass. Counts to three after every chime before looking back.
A Twi'lek woman holds court at the central booth, House Organa sash on her shoulder. Repeats the last word of every sentence in a whisper to herself, then continues. Denies doing it if asked.
A duelling scar at the jaw, civilian black, holding her brandy by the rim. Eyes track every entrance. The two bar stools beside her are empty; nobody has tried to sit there.
The sommelier — a Kel Dor, gloves spotless, decanting cart at his elbow. Pauses a half-beat before any reply, as if translating. Will not pour for a glass with fingerprints on it.
Grey at the temples, a senator's pin at the lapel. Will not say the word 'Empire' — substitutes 'the current administration,' every time, without breaking stride.
A red-faced human in evening wear at the corner booth, talking loudly enough that the servers are giving him space. Repeats his own punchlines, louder each time.
A Falleen in cream silks at the bar, drink untouched, every motion deliberate. Asks the same question three different ways across a conversation — and remembers which version you answered.
A Sullustan clerk at the bar, ledger stylus tucked behind one ear, working through a stack of bond receipts. He has not ordered a second drink.
An Ithorian in plain civilian dress, alone at a small table, working through course three of a quiet meal.
The pianist at the corner instrument, working through a set list pinned to the stand. Does not look at the keys or the room.
A coat-check droid at the entrance, brass plating, single ceremonial epaulette. Hands back garments without a word.
A Devaronian at a two-top, reading a quarterly financial report on a datapad with the small smile of someone whose holdings did well.
'Compliments of a guest who prefers not to be named.' The sommelier sets an unfamiliar bottle at the players' table and waits.

A Zabrak in midnight formalwear vaults the bar in a single motion, lands behind it, takes the bottle she wants and tosses a credit chit back over her shoulder. The bartender catches it without turning.
The maître d' approaches the players' table at an unhurried pace, hands clasped at the small of his back. He has not looked away since he started walking.
A duelling scar at the jaw, removing her gloves at the bar one finger at a time. Two patrons on the next stools have stood and are leaving their drinks unfinished.
A senator in a House Organa sash walks past the players' table and lets a folded flimsi fall from her sleeve onto the empty chair. She does not slow down.
A Mirialan with intricate facial markings has just taken the empty chair at the players' booth. 'Please. Pretend I belong here for thirty seconds.'
An ISB officer in charcoal stands at the entrance, accepting a folded envelope from the maître d' and slipping it inside his tunic without looking down. The maître d' does not see him out.
A flushed human is shouting at his companion in the corner booth, finger jabbing the table. The maître d' is at his shoulder, voice too low to hear, hand resting lightly on his arm.
The bartender slides a drink down the bar. A credit chit is folded under the napkin; the patron pockets it as he lifts the glass.
A Gran in evening wear settles his bill, slides a small lacquered case across the bar with the credit chip, and leaves without a glance back.
A young Rodian server is laughing — actually laughing — at something a regular has said. She catches herself, recovers, refills his glass.
Two senators in matching House sashes share a back booth. One finishes the other's sentences with a half-beat pause for permission, every time, without exception.
A grey-haired man in dress greys and a younger Chiss in civilian formalwear, drinks untouched. They have traded the same identical glance four times in five minutes.
Two Bothans at the mezzanine rail. The older one nods once at the players; the younger looks at her datapad and types a single line.
Two Sullustan executives at a corner booth, datapads between them, working through a contract over cocktails.
A Twi'lek couple at the bar, talking quietly in Ryl, laughing into their glasses. They are holding hands under the bar.
A Mon Calamari accountant and a human auditor share a two-top, datapads turned inward, comparing columns line by line over untouched wine.
Two servers in livery clear a six-top in silence, working from opposite ends and meeting in the middle.
Two elderly humans share a dessert at a window table, his hand over hers, neither speaking. They have been there since the players arrived.
A long table of four Imperial officers in dress greys, drinks untouched, conversation pitched too low to follow.
Three Czerka executives at the central booth, plates cleared, datapads still out, laughing without raising their voices.
Five young humans at the corner booth, all wearing the same House signet on the wrong finger. The whole table goes silent in unison when a server approaches, and resumes the moment she's gone.
Three Aqualish at a mezzanine table raise glasses in a toast, drink, sit back. They have not spoken to each other since they ordered.
A senator at the next booth uses one of the players' names to her companion, then changes the subject before she can be asked how she knows it.
The sommelier passes the players' table twice without acknowledging their empty glasses. On the third pass, he sets down a wine list none of them asked for.
A datachip arrives on the players' table on a folded napkin, no server visible. The napkin has a small embossed crest none of them recognize.
The pianist segues from her standing repertoire into a piece one of the players grew up with — and pauses on the bridge as if waiting for a response.
The maître d' approaches and asks, with perfect courtesy, whether the gentleman who reserved the players' table will be joining them tonight.
A bottle the players did not order arrives at their table. The sommelier is already withdrawing. The card under the bottle reads only: 'We should talk. Upstairs.'
The privacy field at the booth beside the players cuts out. Two senators continue talking for several seconds — names, dates, and a meeting place reach the players' table.
A serving droid sets a second bill on the players' table. The total has tripled. The droid waits, hands folded, until acknowledged.
Three Imperial naval officers in dress uniforms have just entered. The maître d' is leading them directly toward the players' booth.
Every privacy field in the room drops at once. At the entrance, an officer in ISB charcoal is reading from a datapad — the maître d' glances toward the players' booth.
The bartender catches one player's eye, drops her gaze to a holdout blaster set on the inside of the bar, and back up. A patron at the central booth has stood, not turned around.
A senator at a far table collapses face-down into her plate. Her companion stands and walks toward the lift without raising the alarm.
